chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah Most High support him—reported to me, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to him: Inform me about the boundary of the face which should be washed in wudu (ablution), the one Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned. He said: “The face which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded to be washed is that over which no one should add and from which no one should diminish. If he adds to it, he is not rewarded; and if he diminishes from it, he sins. It is that over which the forefinger, middle finger, and thumb pass, from the hairline of the head to the chin; and whatever the two fingers cover of the face in a circular manner, then it is part of the face, and whatever is beyond that is not.” I said: The temple is not part of the face? He said: “No.”
And with this chain, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, who said:

I wrote to al-Riḍā عليه السلام asking him about the boundary of the face, so he wrote back to me: “From the beginning of the hair to the end of the face, and likewise the two sides of the forehead at that point.”

key_terms.الذَّقَنِ: the chin, the lower boundary of the face
key_terms.السَّبَّابَةُ: the forefinger used as a measure for defining the face
key_terms.الْإِبْهَامُ: the thumb used as a measure for defining the face
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face whose limits are being defined for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوُسْطَى: the middle finger used as a measure for defining the face
key_terms.بِغَسْلِهِ: its washing, meaning the required act in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.قُصَاصِ شَعْرِ الرَّأْسِ: the hairline of the head from which the upper boundary begins
key_terms.يُوَضَّأَ: to be washed as part of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What are the boundaries of the face that must be washed in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the legal boundary of the face that must be washed in wudu (ablution). It explains that one must neither exceed nor fall short of the required area, and it gives a practical measure for determining the face’s limits.
